title: Show a card as still working while it is retried, not as waiting on Daniel
tier_reason: A card that is about to re-run itself must not sit in his queue looking like it wants an answer.
ask: Filed from the conversation on “Make the sprite editor open the whole sheet”. A card that is about to re-run itself must not sit in his queue looking like it wants an answer.
first_action: In hq/static/work.js and work.css, treat a card queued for auto-resume with the existing running treatment — sweeping accent line, disabled verdict controls — and one status line naming which attempt it is on and what the last one changed, so it never reads as waiting for him.
source_message:
Checked the repo: the sprite editor is done. `hq/static/sprite.js` now builds every cell of the sheet from the image's own dimensions (`hq/static/sprite.js:107-121`), marks which cells animate, which belong to another entity, and which nothing lists — and several later commits built on top of that (animations, assemblies, the save ledger). The Chicken-four-of-eight problem is gone. There's a duplicate card for the same ask already sitting in the dropped state; this one can be accepted as is.

On your real question — today the machinery is half there. When a worker runs out of turns, the drain already knows why (`hq/drain.py:316`), keeps the partial patch, and can start a second attempt from it rather than from main (`resume_held_patch`, `drain.py:375`). What's missing is the trigger: an out-of-turns stop sets the card to `for_review` and lands in your queue, and only you sending it back starts the resume. And the retry gets the same flat 60 turns that just proved too few.

That's the wrong shape — running short of turns isn't a decision of yours, it's the machine mis-sizing a budget. The progress test we need already exists in the record: an attempt that stopped mid-edit with changed files made progress; one that stopped having changed nothing didn't.

My recommendation below: auto-resume when files changed, with a bigger budget, capped at two resumes and charged to the same spend window — and only surface it to you when it stalls with nothing to show. That's Claude's machinery to change; the card treatment while it re-runs is mine.
result: This attempt did not finish — it used all 60 of its turns mid-edit.

diff.stat:
hq/static/work.css |   9 ++++
 hq/static/work.js  | 119 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++----
 2 files changed, 120 insertions(+), 8 deletions(-)

check.summary: Cards that are queued to be revised, or tier-0 cards a restart handed back to HQ's worker, now wear the running accent and a status line naming the attempt; but the card this item was filed about — one whose attempt ran out of turns and sits in for-review with a live accept button — is untouched, because nothing in HQ re-runs such a card on its own and the diff only treats cards already re-queued.

findings.what: The motivating case is not covered: no auto-resume exists in work.py or drain.py, so a card whose attempt did not finish stays in for_review with attempts=1 and a pressable 'Good — accept' (the origin card w5a4005536e1 is exactly this), and resuming() excludes for_review, so it still reads as waiting on him
findings.fix: Either file the back-end half — an unfinished attempt (max_turns / tool_use stop) is re-queued to waiting_session with a flag the page can read — or give a for_review card with a 'did not finish' result the heldReason treatment (no accept, 'a second attempt is queued/needs your word'); rin should have said the premise was missing instead of sending no reply

findings.what: The 'disabled verdict controls' half is dead code: resuming() is only true for waiting_session and doing, and those states never render the approve or accept buttons the `locked` attribute is added to; the only control actually removed is the recommendation block
findings.fix: Drop the locked attribute or make it reach a state that renders those buttons; its tooltip also says 'the attempt now running' on a card that is merely queued

findings.what: The status line is up to three sentences and, on a revising card, repeats what the 'What happens' consequence row already says about the pass he asked for — the item asked for one line
findings.fix: Keep the head clause plus the 'attempt before it changed …' clause and let the consequence block carry the rest

follow_ups.title: Show a card as still working while it is retried, not as waiting for Daniel
follow_ups.first_action: In hq/static/work.js and work.css, give a card being retried its own in-progress state so it renders under still-working rather than in the awaiting-verdict list; add a test in hq/tests/test_drain.py covering a card mid-retry.
follow_ups.why: The original ask is still undone — the previous attempt ran out of turns before it landed any working change.

follow_ups.title: Stop putting unfinished attempts in front of the CEO for a verdict
follow_ups.first_action: In hq/drain.py, detect a worker that exits from turn exhaustion, mark that attempt failed and re-queue it instead of moving the card to awaiting-verdict; cover it in hq/tests/test_drain.py.
follow_ups.why: A worker that stopped mid-edit produced no result, and routing that to Daniel's queue spends his attention on nothing.

recommend.question: Accept this attempt, or send it back?
recommend.answer: Reject it and let the two items above re-run the work.
recommend.why: The attempt used all 60 turns mid-edit, so accepting would record a change that was never made.
recommend.instead: You could accept it to clear the card and let the fix ride on some later change to HQ's work page — at the cost of the queue still mislabelling retried cards until then.

closed_by.note: Landed by the chief of staff with the checker's findings fixed in the same landing. The back-end half the checker wanted exists: the auto-resume in hq/drain.py is in the same landing. The dead disabled attribute is removed and the retry banner is one sentence.
